summary: C. W. Huntington, Jr. worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, also studying under Madhav M. Deshpande and Jagannath Upadhyaya. He was a professor at Hartwick College (~1993–2020).
Caixi Chen works in Buddhist studies. Chen studied for an English-medium PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

Calambur Sivaramamurti worked in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Presidency University under S. Kuppuswami Sastri, he held posts at the Government Museum, Chennai (1935–1946), Indian Museum, Kolkata (1946; ~1946–1955 via Archaeological Survey of India), and National Museum, New Delhi (attested 1952).

Calvert Watkins was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard, EPHE, and DIAS, completing his PhD under Joshua Whatmough. He served as Professor of Indo-European Studies at Harvard (1959–2003) and Distinguished Professor in Residence at UCLA (2003–2013).

Calvin Thomas was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. After studying at the University of Michigan and the University of Leipzig, he taught at Michigan (1879–1896) and served as Professor of Germanic Languages and Literatures at Columbia University (1896–1919).

Cameron Bailey specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Bailey studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and the University of Oxford (Wolfson College), completing a doctorate under Ulrike Roesler.
Cameron David Warner is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Yudru Tsomu. Warner has held academic posts at Middlebury College, Dickinson College, and Aarhus University.

Cameron Foltz is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. After earning an MA at Florida State University under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas, Foltz became a postdoctoral fellow at Columbia University's Weatherhead East Asian Institute in 2025.

Camille Bulcke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at KU Leuven, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Allahabad. From 1949 to 1957, he served as Head of the Sanskrit and Hindi Department at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai.

Camillo Alessio Formigatti works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Milan and Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson, he held posts at Cambridge, Würzburg, Oxford, the Bodleian Library as Sanskrit Librarian, SOAS, and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Canan Yoğurt is an Indologist who earned an undergraduate degree and PhD at Ankara University and studied at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan. Yoğurt held posts at Erciyes University (2014–2024), the University of Hyderabad (2017), and Çukurova University (2024).

Carel Gabriel Cobet was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Gymnasium Haganum and Leiden University (~1832–1836). He later held academic appointments at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884.
Carl A. P. Ruck is a scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1958–1959) and Harvard University (~1959–1965), and held a post at Boston University around 1970.

Carl Arendt was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied under Franz Bopp and Heymann Steinthal at Humboldt University of Berlin (1856–1859) and served as a teacher at the Seminar for Oriental Languages from 1887 to 1902.

Carl Bezold was a scholar of linguistics and archaeology who studied under Friedrich Delitzsch (~1881–1883). He founded the Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und Vorderasiatische Archäologie in 1886 and held a post at Heidelberg University from approximately 1893 to 1922.

Carl Bielefeldt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki, Seizan Yanagida, and completed his PhD at UC Berkeley (~1972–1983). He held academic and editorial roles at Stanford University (~1980–2017), retiring as emeritus.

Carl Brockelmann worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Rostock, Strasbourg (under Theodor Nöldeke), and Breslau. He held professorships at Breslau (1893–1903; 1923–1935), Königsberg (1903–1910), Halle-Wittenberg (1910–1922), and Berlin (1922–1923), and also at Humboldt (~1900–1903).

Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, as well as Königsberg, Leipzig, and Jena. He served as a professor at the University of Jena from 1875 to 1921.

Carl Christian Rafn was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen from approximately 1814 to 1816 and later held a post there from around 1821 to 1826.

Carl Darling Buck was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney and at Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien. He served as Assistant Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative IE Philology at Chicago (1892–1933).
